sites.operation: STS [R0.X4], R6 (st.shared.f32 into best_dist[thread_idx], predicated on the compare; one unrolled copy per iteration i = 1,2,4,...,512, e.g. i=1: 0x2550, i=32: 0x2940). Companion store on the index array at L55: STS.64 [R0.X8+0x1000], R4 (best_dist_idx[thread_idx], e.g. i=32: 0x2950)

LDS R6, [R0.X4+4*i] (ld.shared.f32 of best_dist[thread_idx + i]; e.g. i=1: 0x2520 [R0.X4+0x4], i=32: 0x2910 [R0.X4+0x80]); the own-slot read best_dist[thread_idx] is LDS R3,[R0.X4]. Companion load on the index array at L55: @P LDS.64 R4, [R0.X8+0x1000+8*i] (best_dist_idx[thread_idx + i], e.g. i=32: 0x2930)

thread_pair_example: driver input: 8 blocks (one per query point) of 1024 threads, one batch of M = 128 reference points whose distance to every query decreases with the index, so thread w < 127 really executes the write at L54 in iterations i with w + i <= 127. Iteration i = 32 of the stride-doubling loop (cross-warp): thread 0 (warp 0) loads best_dist[32] (L53) and best_dist_idx[32] (L55) while thread 32 (warp 1) stores best_dist[32] (L54) and best_dist_idx[32] (L55) in the same barrier interval (the only __syncthreads of an iteration is at the loop top, L51). Likewise thread t (warp t/32) vs thread t+32 for t = 0..63 with writes (t+32 in 32..95). For i < 32 the same pattern occurs intra-warp (e.g. i = 1: thread 0 reads best_dist[1] while thread 1 writes best_dist[1]; no __syncwarp).
class_reason: All four accesses (the best_dist / best_dist_idx loads of slot thread_idx+i and the stores to slot thread_idx) are ordinary shared-memory accesses (plain LDS / STS, no volatile, no atomic, no .STRONG token), by different threads (cross-warp for i >= 32, intra-warp for i < 32) with no barrier between the load of slot s by thread s-i and the store of slot s by thread s in the same iteration: plain-vs-plain unordered conflict, hence data race (DR) under D20; no strong access, so not SC.
buggy_expected: DR on the shared arrays best_dist (L53 load vs L54 store) and best_dist_idx (L55 load vs L55 store): many pairs per barrier interval, cross-warp for i >= 32 and intra-warp for i < 32

fixed.reason: the fix replaces the in-place sliding reduction by a tree reduction (fixed L52-L58): in step u only threads t < THREADS >> (u+1) are active; thread t reads best_dist[idx_1] and best_dist[idx_2] with idx_1 = (2t) << u (even multiple of 2^u) and idx_2 = (2t+1) << u (odd multiple of 2^u) and writes only best_dist[idx_1] / best_dist_idx[idx_1], its own even slot. Within one barrier interval (the __syncthreads at the loop top, fixed L51) the written slots (even multiples of 2^u) are never read by another thread (the reads are of its own idx_1 and of the odd multiples), so read and write sets are disjoint. verify.expected_report_fixed: nothing. (Fixed also changes `continue` to `break` in the batch lookup, unrelated, no shared access.)

open_questions: Which of the pairs a detector reports is not pre-registered beyond DR on best_dist and best_dist_idx. With the driver input (M = 128 reference points) a write by thread w in iteration i needs w + i <= 127 and a reader thread w - i >= 0, so the cross-warp iteration with executed writes is i = 32 only (writers w = 32..95, readers t = w - 32 = 0..63); iterations i = 1..16 give intra-warp pairs, i >= 64 execute no racy write for this input (a larger M, argument 2 of the driver, would add i = 64, 128, ...).
